Venison Pies

Served at: St. Andrew's Day

Serves 6Prep 30 minCook 1 hr 30 min

Venison pies are a traditional Scottish dish often enjoyed on St. Andrew's Day, a celebration of Scotland's patron saint. These hearty pies showcase rich, gamey venison combined with savory herbs and vegetables, encased in a buttery pastry, making them perfect for the chilly November festivities.

Ingredients

  • 2 lbs (900 g) venison shoulder or stewing meat, cut into 1-inch cubes
  • 2 tablespoons vegetable oil
  • 1 large onion, finely chopped
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 2 medium carrots, diced
  • 2 celery stalks, diced
  • 1 cup (240 ml) beef or venison stock
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) red wine
  • 2 tablespoons tomato paste
  • 1 teaspoon dried thyme
  • 1 teaspoon dried rosemary
  • 1 bay leaf
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
  • 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour
  • 1 package (14 oz/400 g) refrigerated pie crusts or homemade shortcrust pastry
  • 1 egg, beaten (for egg wash)

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
  2. Heat the vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
  3. Add the venison cubes and brown them on all sides; remove and set aside.
  4. In the same pot, add the onion, garlic, carrots, and celery; cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
  5. Return the venison to the pot and sprinkle the flour over the meat and vegetables; stir well to coat evenly.
  6. Add the tomato paste, dried thyme, rosemary, bay leaf, red wine, and stock; stir to combine.
  7. Bring the mixture to a simmer, cover, and cook on low heat for about 1 hour, or until the venison is tender and the sauce has thickened. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
  8. Remove the bay leaf and let the filling cool slightly.
  9. Roll out one pie crust and line six individual pie tins or one large pie dish.
  10. Fill the crusts with the venison filling.
  11. Cover with the second pie crust, trim excess pastry, and crimp the edges to seal.
  12. Cut small slits in the top of each pie to allow steam to escape.
  13. Brush the tops with beaten egg for a golden finish.
  14. Bake in the preheated oven for 30-35 minutes, or until the pastry is golden brown and crisp.
  15. Remove from the oven and let cool for 5 minutes before serving.

Tips

  • For extra flavor, marinate the venison in red wine and herbs overnight before cooking.
  • Serve with traditional Scottish sides like mashed potatoes and steamed greens.
  • Leftover pies can be reheated in the oven to retain crispness.
